title: Business Combination — Goodwill and NCI at Acquisition (full-goodwill method)
scenario: On the acquisition date, Meridian Building Group acquires 80% of the voting stock of Cobalt Fabrication for $4,000,000 cash. Cobalt's identifiable net assets have a book value of $3,500,000 and a fair value of $4,200,000; the entire $700,000 difference relates to an undervalued building. Meridian measures the non-controlling interest at fair value (the full-goodwill method), and the fair value of the 20% NCI is $1,000,000. Round to the nearest dollar.

tasks.prompt: Requirement 1 — Compute the acquisition-date fair value of Cobalt as a whole under the full-goodwill method.
tasks.explanation: Under the full-goodwill (fair-value) method, the acquiree's total fair value = consideration transferred for the controlling interest $4,000,000 + fair value of the NCI $1,000,000 = $5,000,000.
Total goodwill = acquiree fair value $5,000,000 − fair value of identifiable net assets $4,200,000 = $800,000.

tasks.prompt: Requirement 3 — Compute the acquisition-date fair-value adjustment to the identifiable net assets (the building step-up).
tasks.explanation: The fair-value step-up = fair value $4,200,000 − book value $3,500,000 = $700,000, allocated to the undervalued building on the consolidated balance sheet.

tasks.prompt: Requirement 4 — Compute the NCI's share of goodwill and the parent's share of goodwill.
tasks.explanation: NCI goodwill = NCI fair value $1,000,000 − 20% × identifiable net assets fair value $4,200,000 ($840,000) = $160,000. Parent goodwill = total goodwill $800,000 − NCI goodwill $160,000 = $640,000.
